definitions.explanation: A stick of calcium carbonate or gypsum used for writing on blackboards. The standard word for classroom chalk in Japanese.

examples.japanese: チョークで{字|じ}を{書|か}く。
{白|しろ}いチョークが{折|お}れてしまった。
{先生|せんせい}が{黒板|こくばん}にチョークで{数式|すうしき}を{書|か}いている。
examples.english: The teacher is writing a mathematical formula on the blackboard with chalk.

examples.japanese: チョークの{粉|こな}で{手|て}が{白|しろ}くなった。
examples.english: My hands turned white from chalk dust.

notes:
A loanword from English "chalk." This is the standard word used in Japanese schools. Although many Japanese classrooms have shifted to whiteboards and markers, chalk and blackboards remain common, especially in public schools.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- チョークで{書|か}く: to write with chalk
- チョークの{粉|こな}: chalk dust
- {色|いろ}チョーク: colored chalk
- チョークを{持|も}つ: to hold chalk
- チョーク{入|い}れ: chalk holder/case

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {白墨|はくぼく}: chalk — the Sino-Japanese term; formal and somewhat old-fashioned
- マーカー: marker — used on whiteboards, the modern alternative

CULTURAL NOTE:
The phrase チョーク{芸|げい} (chalk art) refers to the skill of drawing impressive diagrams or illustrations on a blackboard, valued among Japanese teachers.
